intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene (615618) on chromosome 3q13.33.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing data analysis identified nine missense and one nonsense recessive variants (homozygous or compound heterozygous) in the POGLUT1 gene, in 15 patients from nine independent families
checks.explanation: Recessive homozygous/compound heterozygous POGLUT1 variants cause LGMD R21.

checks.claim: The POGLUT1 gene is located on chromosome 3q13.33.
checks.evidence_quote: A biallelic mutation in the POGLUT1 gene has been reported in one family as the cause of an adult-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD R21; OMIM# 617232).
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is a slowly progressive muscular dystrophy in which proximal weakness mainly affects the lower limbs. Onset is usually in adulthood, but congenital and infantile onset have been reported. Muscle biopsy shows hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan and fewer satellite cells than normal. Muscle imaging shows a distinctive 'inside-to-outside' pattern of fatty degeneration in the thigh muscles (Servián-Morilla et al., 2020).

checks.claim: LGMDR21 is a slowly progressive muscular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The weakness showed a proximal distribution, with a clear predominance in the lower limbs and slow progression.

checks.claim: In LGMDR21, proximal weakness mainly affects the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: The weakness showed a proximal distribution, with a clear predominance in the lower limbs and slow progression.

checks.claim: Onset of LGMDR21 is usually in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified one patient with a congenital presentation, two patients with infantile onset before 3 years of age, and 12 patients with adult onset

checks.claim: Congenital and infantile onset of LGMDR21 have been reported.
checks.evidence_quote: However, the age at onset was broadened from adult to congenital and infantile onset.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in LGMDR21 shows hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan.
checks.evidence_quote: Immunofluorescence staining with an antibody against glycosylated α-dystroglycan revealed a reduction of the glycosylated form of α-dystroglycan at the sarcolemma in all muscle biopsies

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reported 15 patients with LGMDR21 from 9 unrelated families from Spain, Bulgaria, Italy, Germany, the USA, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates. Four of the families were consanguineous. Onset was congenital in 1 patient, infantile (before age 3 years) in 2, and adult in 12. Weakness was proximal, predominated in the lower limbs, and progressed slowly. Seven patients whose disease began in their teens needed a wheelchair between the third and fifth decades. Eleven patients had mild to moderate scapular winging. From their mid-forties onward, 6 patients had mild to severe respiratory involvement, regardless of age at onset, and 2 of them used ventilatory support at night. None of the patients had significant bulbar, cardiac, or other systemic manifestations. Serum CK was normal in most patients. The authors noted that this helps distinguish LGMDR21 from most other recessive LGMDs.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reviewed lower limb muscle MRI or CT in 11 of the 15 patients. All 11 showed an 'inside-to-outside' pattern of fatty degeneration. The first areas affected were the inner segments of the vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, and vastus intermedius, the posterior thigh compartment, and the gastrocnemius. Lower leg muscles were better preserved than thigh muscles. The pattern was clearest early in the disease, but it could still be seen in the vastus lateralis at end stage.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) examined muscle biopsies from 9 patients in 6 families. Vastus lateralis biopsies were dystrophic. Biceps brachii biopsies showed mild myopathic features, and some contained lobulated fibers. On immunostaining, glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan was reduced at the sarcolemma in all biopsies, while staining for the alpha-dystroglycan core was normal. Western blots confirmed the hypoglycosylation and showed reduced laminin binding. Patient muscle also had reduced NOTCH1 intracellular domain (NICD) and significantly fewer PAX7-positive satellite cells (5 patients vs 5 controls). There were no or very few eMHC-positive regenerating fibers, whereas disease controls had many.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) studied 15 patients with LGMDR21 from 9 families. Using next-generation sequencing (gene panels or whole-exome sequencing) with Sanger confirmation, they identified 9 missense mutations and 1 nonsense mutation in the POGLUT1 gene, in the homozygous or compound heterozygous state. In every family the variants segregated with disease, and no asymptomatic carriers were found. The novel variants were either absent from ExAC or seen in the heterozygous state in no more than 2 of more than 60,000 non-Finnish European controls.

paragraphs.text: In the patient with congenital onset (family 2, II.1), Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) used NGS panel sequencing to identify 2 POGLUT1 variants, D233E and R279Q. The clinical table and the myoblast experiments describe him as compound heterozygous. R279Q had previously been reported in the heterozygous state in a patient with Dowling-Degos disease. Based on the protein structure, R279Q was predicted to interfere with donor substrate binding. The patient's myoblasts proliferated less and differentiated faster than controls.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) identified homozygous missense mutations in several further families: I129T in the man with infantile onset (family 3), R98W in 3 sisters with adult onset (family 4), Y57C in a woman with adult onset (family 5), W308L in a 22-year-old man with adult onset (family 6), C102F in a 59-year-old man with onset in the fourth decade (family 7), and R183W in the man with infantile onset (family 9). In 2 brothers with adult onset (family 8), they found compound heterozygous mutations: Y156N and a nonsense mutation, c.552G-A (W184X). Functional studies are given for each mutation in the allelic variant paragraphs. In HEK293T cells, mutant protein secretion was tested, along with rescue of Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells, in vitro enzyme activity, and rescue of myogenesis in Drosophila.

(2020) suggested that reduced Notch1 signaling disturbs satellite cell biology and causes the dystrophy. They proposed that hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan contributes as a secondary defect.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) cultured primary myoblasts from the patient compound heterozygous for D233E and R279Q. Compared with controls, these cells proliferated less, had fewer proliferating and self-renewing (PAX7+) cells, had more differentiating cells, and showed increased myogenin expression and fusion index. The authors concluded that slow proliferation and facilitated myogenic differentiation underlie POGLUT1-related muscular dystrophy.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) proposed that LGMDR21 be considered, and POGLUT1 sequenced, in patients with recessive LGMD who have the following features: alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation, reduced PAX7+ cells, and reduced NICD levels on muscle biopsy, together with the inside-to-outside MRI pattern. They noted that this pattern must be distinguished from collagen VI myopathy, in which the outer areas of the vastus lateralis degenerate first. They also pointed out that serum CK is normal in most patients.

checks.evidence_quote: when a patient with a recessive form of LGMD shows a combination of α-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation, reduction of PAX7+ cells and NICD levels in the muscle biopsy, and the above-mentioned muscle MRI pattern, a diagnosis of LGMD R21 should be considered and the POGLUT1 gene should be sequenced

checks.evidence_quote: Another diagnostic hint was that most cases showed normal CK levels.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) tested patient variants in a Drosophila myogenesis rescue assay in rumi(79/79) flies. Wildtype human POGLUT1 fully rescued the shortened indirect flight muscles. D233E, R183W, I129T, and Y57C were expressed at normal levels but gave only partial rescue, and C102F gave no rescue. The authors concluded that all variants tested reduce the myogenic activity of POGLUT1.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found a homozygous ile129-to-thr (I129T) mutation in the POGLUT1 gene in a 46-year-old man with infantile-onset LGMDR21 (family 3). He used a wheelchair from age 33. The variant was absent from ExAC. In HEK293T cells, the mutant protein was poorly secreted and was not detected in cell lysates, suggesting severe destabilization. It did not rescue Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells. In Drosophila, the mutant was expressed normally but only partially rescued myogenesis.
